cse-2014-1-cs-4.approach: Four equations in three unknowns: check whether one equation depends on the others. Here eq.2 − eq.4 gives eq.1, so the system reduces to three independent equations with a unique solution.

steps.body: $(4x + 7z) - (x - 2y + 7z) = 1 - 0 \Rightarrow 3x + 2y = 1$, which is exactly eq.1. So eq.1 is redundant and the system is consistent.

steps.title: Solve the remaining three
steps.body:
From eq.1: $y = \frac{1 - 3x}{2}$; from eq.2: $z = \frac{1 - 4x}{7}$. Substitute in $x + y + z = 3$ and multiply by 14:
$$14x + 7(1 - 3x) + 2(1 - 4x) = 42$$
$$14x + 7 - 21x + 2 - 8x = 42 \Rightarrow -15x = 33 \Rightarrow x = -2.2$$
Then $y = \frac{1 + 6.6}{2} = 3.8$, $z = \frac{1 + 8.8}{7} = 1.4$.

steps.title: Conclude
steps.body: Rank of coefficient matrix = rank of augmented matrix = 3 = number of unknowns ⇒ exactly **1** solution.

pitfalls: Assuming 4 equations in 3 unknowns must be inconsistent (0 solutions).

cse-2014-1-cs-5.approach: Eigenvectors of a real symmetric matrix belonging to distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal, so their dot product is 0. Positive definiteness is irrelevant here.

steps.body:
Let $Ax = \lambda x$, $Ay = \mu y$, $\lambda \ne \mu$, $A = A^T$. Then
$$\lambda\, x^T y = (Ax)^T y = x^T A^T y = x^T A y = \mu\, x^T y$$

steps.title: Conclude
steps.body: $(\lambda - \mu)\, x^T y = 0$ and $\lambda \ne \mu$ ⇒ $x \cdot y = 0$.

so $f$ is not constant on the interval; a non-constant differentiable function cannot have $f' \equiv 0$. Hence some $\theta$ has $f'(\theta) \ne 0$. ✔
